title: Da Nang food: 6 dishes to try

scenes.narration: What to eat in Da Nang? Here are six dishes you have to try, with where they come from, how they are made, how to eat them, and places checked on Google Maps.
scenes.label: REGIONAL FOOD
scenes.caption: DA NANG
scenes.tip: Origin · How it's made · How to eat · Where

scenes.narration: Dish one, mi Quang. Its origin is still debated, but it is tied to noodle villages on the Thu Bon river, such as Phu Chiem. The rice noodles are steamed as sheets, cut wide and often tinted yellow with turmeric. There is only a splash of broth, with shrimp and pork or chicken. To eat it, crumble a sesame rice cracker on top, add herbs, peanuts, lime and chili, and mix it all. Try Hong Nga, Co Sau, or My Son.
scenes.caption: Mì Quảng

scenes.narration: Dish two, pork rice paper rolls. Nobody knows who first made them. They were once known only in Quang Nam and Da Nang, and are now a local specialty. Pork is boiled or steamed and sliced thin, best with dew-softened rice paper from Dai Loc. To eat, lay out the rice paper, add herbs and pork, roll it tight, and dip it in fermented fish sauce with pineapple and chili. Try Com Dai Loc, Donald Trung, or Bep Be Anh.

scenes.narration: Dish three, fish cake noodle soup. Da Nang sits right by the sea, so fresh fish is everywhere and fish cake became a breakfast staple. Mackerel or lizardfish is pounded with seasoning, kneaded until springy, then steamed or fried golden. The broth is simmered from fish bones with pumpkin, pineapple and tomato. To eat, add pickled shallots and chili garlic, and a little shrimp paste if you like. Try Di Tam or Ma Hai.

scenes.narration: Dish four, noodles with fermented fish sauce. Mam nem is a specialty of the central coast, made from sea fish salted and fermented for a long time. The bowl has boiled pork, roast pork, pork roll, shredded papaya, young jackfruit and herbs. To eat, pour on the sauce mixed with pineapple and chili, then toss everything well. Try Liem, Hong, or Be Ha.

scenes.narration: Dish five, central style crispy pancakes, smaller and crunchier than the southern kind. Rice batter with turmeric goes into a hot pan with shrimp, pork and bean sprouts, and fries until golden. What sets them apart is the thick dipping sauce made from liver, peanuts and sesame. To eat, wrap a pancake in rice paper with herbs and grilled pork skewers, then dip. Try Banh Xeo seventy six, a Michelin Bib Gourmand pick, Ba Tuyet, or Banh Xeo Lang.

scenes.narration: Dish six, Nam O raw fish salad, from the fishing village of Nam O at the foot of the Hai Van pass. Fresh herring is boned and sliced, then marinated with ginger, galangal, garlic and toasted rice powder. The dip is cooked from the fish juices with Nam O fish sauce, chili and tapioca starch, topped with sesame and peanuts. To eat, roll the fish with wild herbs in rice paper and dip. Try A Sinh, Co Hong, or Goi Ca Mien Trung.
